question.text: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of this Asian country, the center of a former empire led by Genghis Khan.
question.clue: The prince Kul Tigin is honored by 7th century inscriptions named for a river valley in this country's west, the Orkhon, which was a power center for the Gokturk state.

swap.text: Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.
swap.answerHtml: Caspian Sea [or Kaspii Tenizi, or Hazar Denzi, or Hezer Denizi]
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: As a child, this person defeated their blood brother Jamukha and rescued their kidnapped wife Borte ["BOHR-tay"] from a rival tribe.
question.text: Name this person, who ruled the largest contiguous empire in history. This person born with the name Temujin was succeeded by their son Ogedei.
question.clue: He also defeated both the Xi Xia and Jin Dynasties, and after his death, he was succeeded not by Jochi or Chatagai, but by his third son, Ogodai.

swap.leadin: Following this man's brutal sack of Baghdad, he had human skulls stacked into giant pyramids.
swap.text: Name this famously handicapped Central Asian conqueror of Mongol origin who conquered a massive empire before suddenly dying en route to an invasion of China.
swap.clue: This man's victories at the Battles of the Kondurcha and Terek Rivers led to his defeat of Tokhtamysh and the Golden Horde.

question.text: Under the Timurid Empire, Samarkand became a center of this trade route which connected Europe to Asia. Traders on this route named for a certain textile stopped at caravanserais.
question.clue: In the plural, this term was subtitled A New History of the World in a work by Peter Frankopan, and it names Yo-Yo Ma's ensemble to promote cross-cultural artistic collaboration.

swap.leadin: This man earned his epithet after he suffered an injury while serving in Khorasan.
swap.text: Name this Turkic conqueror who ruled a successor state to the Chagatai Khanate from Samarkand. He was interred in a jade tomb after his death.
swap.answerHtml: Tamerlane [or Timur the Lame or Taimur Lang or Timur Gurkani or Taimur Gurkani]
swap.clue: After detaining an envoy sent by the Emperor Hongwu, he led a short lived expedition against the Ming Dynasty.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about notable "salt roads" across world history.
question.text: In the 20th century, a major Himalayan salt road connected this region and Nepal. This region's spiritual leader is the Dalai Lama.
question.clue: A religious leader from this country formerly ruled from the Potala Palace but now lives in exile in India.

swap.leadin: This conflict began when Lord Ellenborough sought to establish a trade route to Bukhara.
swap.text: Name this 19th-century diplomatic and political conflict that resulted in the creation of the Wakhan Corridor and the Durand Line on the northern border of British India.
swap.answerHtml: Great Game [prompt on, but do NOT reveal, answers that mention Russia invading Afghanistan or Britain invading Afghanistan by asking “what broader conflict was that was part of?”; do NOT accept or prompt on “the Soviet Union invading Afghanistan” or equivalents]
swap.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

question.leadin: A faction of bandits led by Habibullah Kalakani in this country was named the Saqqawists, deriving from his nickname as the son of a water carrier.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose emirate was once ruled by the Durrani family. William Elphinstone led a British retreat from this country.
question.clue: This country's border with its eastern neighbor became the Durand Line after the Treaty of Rawalpindi, and Elphinstone's column was lost on a retreat from this country.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
swap.text: Primarily made up of three groups the Uzbeks, the Hazara, and the Tajiks, members of this military and political organization aided in overthrowing the Taliban and found key positions in Hamid Karzai's government.
swap.answerHtml: The Northern Alliance [or The United Front for the Salvation of Afghanistan; or the UIF]

question.leadin: His army built pyramids of human skulls after sacking Delhi.
question.text: Name this Central Asian warlord who conquered most of the Middle East and Central Asia in the late 14th century. This warlord, whose namesake dynasty was centered in Samarkand, was nicknamed "the Lame."
question.clue: The only time an Ottoman Sultan was captured in battle was duringthis man's victory at the Battle of Ankara against Bayezid Thunderbolt.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
swap.text: In the late 9th century, the Alans established an independent kingdom in this mountain range. A nation in this range is often recognized as the first to establish Christianity as its official religion, doing so in 301 A.D.
swap.clue: Gold and silver tubes, possibly used to drink beer, that were found in this region were made by the Maykop culture, which, like this region's Kura-Araxes culture, constructed burial mounds called kurgans.

question.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the antics of the Taliban.
swap.text: The Taliban evolved in response to these Anti-Soviet guerilla fighters from the 1980's, who took their name from the Arabic word for "strugglers."
swap.clue: A manual titled for the "victory" of people known by this word prescribed 200 men to fill each "cushoon" operating rocket artillery in Tipu Sultan's Mysorean army.

question.text: Once the Red Army toppled Ungern von Sternberg, this early Mongolian leader liquidated Mongolian Buddhist institutions and clergy after pushing out Peljidiin Genden, who had denied Stalin's requests to do so.
question.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

swap.leadin: Of the 16,000-plus men to begin a journey from this city, only assistant surgeon William Brydon survived to reach Jalalabad (juh-LAHL-uh-bad).
swap.text: Name this city from which Lord Elphinstone led a disastrous retreat in 1842. In modern times, the Saur (SAH-wur) Revolution ended after Sardar Daud Khan was assassinated in this capital city.
swap.clue: A mid-1990s siege of this city culminated in the hanging of former president Mohammad Najibullah outside the Arg Presidential Palace.

question.leadin: A traveler displays his sextant and compass to this city's "Koosh Begee" upon being asked of his scientific prowess in an account by Sir Alexander Burnes.
question.text: Name this city in Central Asia. The Manghit Dynasty ruled an Emirate named for this city in Transoxiana, which was also the capital of the Samanid Dynasty.
question.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

swap.text: The Gokturks were led by this tribe and ruling dynasty. This tribe had been subjugated by the Rouran in 460, but conquered them in 552 under the leadership of Bumin Qaghan.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British boondoggles in Afghanistan in the 19th century.
question.text: This "line" was set up to divide Afghanistan and British India by an 1893 treaty between the namesake British foreign secretary and the Afghani ruler Amir Abdur Khan. After the partition of India, it became the line between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.leadin: Members of this ethnicity formed a 300-year confederation with the Cumans, with whom they are sometimes identified.
swap.text: Identify this ethnicity of Baibars and most rulers of the Bahri dynasty.
